Fallback trigger is `invalid_prompt`-specific: Approach — 'only if the post-merge dispatch run's openai job is again rejected with invalid_prompt'; a missing-model error is a different failure class the condition does not cover
findings.finding: gpt-5.5's presence on the repository's own OPENAI_API_KEY account is unverified (the recorded GET /v1/models verification on 2026-08-03 covered only gpt-5.4/-mini/-nano) and confirmation is deferred to the live run — but the fallback trigger in the AC fires only on another `invalid_prompt`. findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — final [non-codebase] bullet ('If instead it is rejected again ... with invalid_prompt ...') and Approach fallback bullet

Plan's own contrast: GPT-6 'profiles them as non-reasoning (wrong request shape)'; gpt-5.6-* 'its pinned profile disagrees with upstream's current one' — showing profile resolution is model-name-sensitive and not uniform across 5.x ids

pydantic_ai.profiles.openai.openai_model_profile EXISTS in the environment but its source is not readable from the repo-scoped tools; no probe output (e.g., the resolved profile for gpt-5.5) is recorded in the plan or ticket — Partially-verified: the integration exists, the specific gpt-5.5 surface is unconfirmed
findings.finding: The plan depends on the pinned pydantic-ai-slim 1.107.9 resolving openai-responses:gpt-5.5 to the SAME reasoning-model profile as gpt-5.4 (same sampling / encrypted-reasoning / structured-output request shape), but this profile-resolution is asserted, not observed. pydantic-ai selects an OpenAI model profile by matching the model-name string; the plan itself notes GPT-6 ids fall into a non-reasoning profile ('wrong request shape') and gpt-5.6-* 'disagrees with upstream'. A profile mismatch for gpt-5.5 would silently send the wrong request shape rather than fail loudly.
findings.location: Approach — 'The pinned pydantic-ai-slim 1.107.9 gives gpt-5.5 exactly the same OpenAI profile as gpt-5.4 ... so only the model id changes.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the causal theory for why moving to gpt-5.5 should evade the invalid_prompt flag given byte-identical requests (e.g. the usage-policy classifier is tied to the model/deployment, not the prompt content), or reframe the change as an explicit try-then-fallback whose success probability is not asserted.
evidence: Root cause states 'The rejections come from OpenAI's side; rebar's requests did not change' with identical body hashes at c43d9336262/0f409b946e4/872e7f6c3fd across green and red
'In the same dispatch run, test_workflow_live sent the same requests for the same fixture plan and passed' — i.e. identical content was accepted elsewhere
The gpt-5.5 bullet argues only that gpt-5.5 has the SAME OpenAI profile / request shape as gpt-5.4 — which, if anything, supports the content being unchanged across the model switch
ABSENCE: no stated rationale that the usage-policy classifier keys on model id rather than prompt content
findings.finding: The plan does not state WHY swapping only the model id (gpt-5.4 -> gpt-5.5) should change OpenAI's verdict, given its own root-cause evidence that the rejected requests are byte-identical across green/red runs and that the SAME requests passed in test_workflow_live in the same dispatch run. The fitness-for-purpose of the primary change rests on an unstated assumption that the invalid_prompt usage-policy flag is model-id-specific rather than content-specific; if the flag is content-based, gpt-5.5 would be rejected identically and only the fallback would resolve the problem.
findings.location: Approach section, 'Model: gpt-5.5' bullet; and Context root-cause ('rebar's requests did not change ... identical full-body hashes')
scenarios: If OpenAI's invalid_prompt flag is content/classifier-based, the post-merge dispatch run's openai job is rejected again and the primary change changed nothing
